claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments - a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed".
- Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
- Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town: Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is part of the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023.
- Judge temporarily blocks Trump from closing Washington DC golf course for renovation: It is the latest development in a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links.
- Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.
- 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".
- Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia: Front-runner Carmelle emerges victorious with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.
- Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress': Sotheby's says it will work with the heirs of a family who had previously owned the artwork to try and reach a solution.
- Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever: The 52-year-old general’s provocative posts and military threats have fuelled rumours of a dynastic succession.
- Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude: The foreign ministry in Abuja says 6 Nigerians with underlying health problems have died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.
- Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.
- 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop: Passengers throughout the country were impacted over what the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) describes as “safety and communication issues”.

image_provider.prompt: A frayed copper wire splitting into two paths—one leading upward toward a gleaming rocket caught mid-air by mechanical hands, the other descending into shadow and uncertainty. Bold, geometric shapes. High contrast. The wire itself forms the central composition, thick and prominent, with sharp angular light suggesting both breakthrough and breakdown. Duotone-friendly: strong silhouettes, minimal detail.
